name: Clear nail polish / buffing shine

image.caption: Thin film of clear nail polish on black card

lead: A buffed or clear-coated nail has an even, glossy surface that reads as neat and well kept, which is why it is used as a low-key male manicure. A nail buffer smooths ridges and adds shine; clear polish adds a lasting coat of gloss.
It is a grooming finish rather than a treatment: the payoff is tidier-looking hands, with no colour that would stand out.

paras: People buff the nail surface with a buffer block to create shine, or brush on a coat of clear polish or top coat. Both are done as part of a regular manicure alongside trimming and cuticle care.
Over-buffing can thin the nail plate, and polish can irritate skin or cause allergic reactions in some people. Salon tools need proper sanitation to avoid infection.[1]

chain: Buff or coat the nail with clear polish
Hands look groomed without visible colour
angle.text: Buffing smooths and shines the nail; clear polish adds a lasting gloss. Both give a natural, groomed look.

lead: Clear nail polish and buffing are two ways of giving fingernails a natural gloss. A nail buffer, one of the standard manicure tools, polishes the nail surface, while clear polish or a top coat adds a transparent glossy layer.[1]

The appeal in male grooming is that the result looks like healthy nails rather than a visibly manicured set. The French manicure, created by Jeff Pink of ORLY in 1976, shows how long a natural nail look has been in demand in the industry.[1]

Clear polish also appears in medical and research settings. A randomized trial in 50 volunteers found that clear and red polish and acrylic nails did not significantly change pulse oximeter readings, while black and brown polish did.[2]
infobox: Nail buffer, clear polish or top coat[1]

paras: A manicure typically uses a buffer among its tools, and base and top coats among its supplies.[1] Clear polish is applied like coloured polish but leaves the nail's own colour visible.

No studies found on clear polish or buffing for appearance. Clear polish has been used in other research settings. A randomized trial in 50 volunteers found clear polish, red polish and acrylic nails did not significantly change Lifebox pulse oximeter readings, while black and brown polish did.[2] A 2023 case report described an eyelid molluscum lesion in an 8-year-old that resolved after four topical nail polish applications over six weeks.[3]
Poor sanitation in manicure settings can cause serious problems, according to the Wikipedia overview of manicure.[1]
